Groomers

Armada delivers a carving monster with the award-winning Declivity 92 Ti. The heat-treated edge is sensitive, and a full-length sidewall provides consistent edge hold. These features, combined with the relatively stiff, progressive flex of the core, deliver the energy that had us craving the next carved turn.

The sidewall is thicker underfoot and tapers toward the tip and tail, allowing easier turn initiation while maintaining strong grip underfoot. The additional torsional rigidity of the full-length sidewall amplified our team's confidence to tip the Declivity 92 Ti way over on its edge.

With a stated 18-meter turn radius, this ski isn't in the same ballpark as a Giant Slalom ski, even if it sometimes felt that way at speed. More like a slalom ski, the Declivity 92 Ti exited turns just as smoothly as it entered them. It was incredibly quick edge-to-edge, with a very precise feeling when it hooked up to start the turn. Thanks to the tapered sidewall, it then finished turns exactly where you wanted.


Variable Snow

This ski crushes through ugly snow. Thanks to a layer of titanal over a coruba core, it provides a stiff, progressive lateral flex, while a sidewall that runs the length of the ski adds maximum torsional rigidity. The combination of titanal and elastomers dampens the ride without eliminating rebound energy.

Many companies are now incorporating these specific types of material blends into the cores of their skis, including other skis in our lineup. Armada claims that this design equates to “more horsepower with a livelier response” – our testers absolutely agree with this description.

The best example of this is when the Declivity 92 Ti transitions from easy-going to difficult conditions. Despite changes in the snow surface, you can keep doing exactly what you want instead of responding to what the ski dictates. In a word, one of our testers described the Declivity 92 Ti as “agile” through crud.


Powder

We're impressed with the versatility of Armada's modern all-mountain ski. Even with its relatively narrow waist width, the Declivity 92 Ti performs admirably in soft snow and even in deep powder. There are always compromises in ski design, but this ski's tip shape and progressive flex provide just enough float to keep the good times rolling.

For seasoned powder skiers, our testers agree the Declivity 92 Ti has just enough rocker and tip width to push through the deep stuff. The ski flexes and reacts predictably, even if the top sheets are generally lost underneath the fluff.

With its tendency to sink in deep powder, the Declivity 92 Ti required aggressive maneuvers to keep it closer to the surface. While expert skiers can pivot this ski through powder, it will be much harder for intermediates due to the relatively small sweet spot in the shovel.


Stability

The Declivity 92 Ti remains poised and agile at high speed, regardless of snow conditions or terrain. Even with a smaller sweet spot than many other skis we tested, one of our testers aptly commented that this ski “seems to have the personality of a GS ski”. The Declivity 92 Ti stays connected to the snow, even through divots and undulating terrain, and maintains supreme composure at any speed.

The 100% coruba core is relatively simple compared to the complex blends other brands are using, but the articulated titanal banding – what Armada dubs ATB technology – is fairly unique. The combination of titanal and elastomer helps reduce chatter, although a few of our testers still noticed some tip rattle that they could feel vibrating into the ski's forebody. They noted, however, that any vibrations are minor, especially compared to other comparable skis we tested.


Playfulness

The specific design of the Declivity 92 Ti tailors the hybrid rocker-camber profile to a tapered sidecut, keeping it playful and fun regardless of snow conditions. However, the skis' small sweet spot underfoot requires at least an advanced skier to unlock its potential.

It's particularly deft in the air and lands with grace. The front of the ski is supportive enough if you happen to land a little too far forward, while the tail is forgiving enough if you end up in the backseat. Even though it's more difficult to make shorter-radius or pivoted turns with this ski, it's still possible with enough athleticism. Even though smearing turns takes focus, it's still very doable and speaks to the ski's balanced nature.


Forgiveness

When it came to skiing moguls, one tester suggested that a skier could just ram it into bumps and have enough faith in the design to deal with the outcome. That might sound a bit ridiculous, but the combination of design and technology makes the Declivity 92 Ti surprisingly forgiving for such a powerful ski.

That said, the skier also needs the strength and skill to handle the rebound. The Declivity 92 Ti is far from a beginner-friendly ski – it may be surprisingly easygoing, but that's only underfoot of advanced to expert skiers.


Should You Buy the Armada Declivity 92 Ti?

The Decilvity 92 Ti is exceptionally good at carving, yet remarkably solid in powder – especially for a 92-millimeter ski. It busts through crud with ease, yet is playful enough to find the fun in any terrain. It's the width of a frontside ski, with the capability of an all-mountain ski and all the personality of a freeride ski. The Declivity 92 Ti s a must-consider for the aggressive, advanced-to-expert-level skier who enjoys exploring the whole mountain.

What Other Skis Should You Consider?

The Declivity 92 Ti is a beefy ski with a healthy dose of personality. It's not quite as stable as the similarly high-scoring Volkl M7 Mantra, but it is slightly more fun. If you're a lighter body type or you're looking to cruise rather than charge, the Fischer Ranger 96 is a more forgiving ski with a similarly playful attitude. And if you're in it for skiing powder, we'll point you to the Blizzard Rustler 9.
